intro: Compton Dundon, a village near Street in Somerset, has a hollow male yew in the churchyard of St Andrew's that was already called very old in the 1780s. Edmund Rack measured it at 23 feet round then, and modern recorders find almost the same. It stands inside a low wall south-south-east of the church, in a churchyard that is open and free. Buses from Street and Somerton run through the village.
meta_description: Edmund Rack measured the hollow Compton Dundon yew in the 1780s, and it has barely changed. Its disputed age and where it stands at St Andrew's.
question_meta: Compton Dundon's oldest tree is the hollow yew at St Andrew's church, probably over 800 years old by the Ancient Yew Group, with claims up to 1,700.
question_answer: The oldest tree in Compton Dundon is the hollow yew in St Andrew's churchyard, 742 centimetres round. The Ancient Yew Group's girth classes put it at probably over 800 years. Locally it was credited with about 1,000 years in 1954, and Wikipedia says over 1,700, but none of these is a dating.
question_context: Few churchyard yews have a measurement as old as this one. Edmund Rack, who died in 1787, surveyed the churchyard and described a very old yew with a fine top, its body hollow and measuring 23 feet in circumference. Two centuries later Tim Hills recorded 24 feet 9 inches at ground level in 2000, and Peter Norton found 23 feet 9 in 2014. The Ancient Yew Group's figure is 742 centimetres, taken 30 centimetres above the ground. The ages offered for it vary a great deal. The Group's girth classes put a yew of this size at probably over 800 years, which is an estimate from size. In 1954 the Rev. R. Kelland recorded that it was locally credited with about 1,000 years. Wikipedia gives over 1,700 years without a source. We report all three, and the plain conclusion that it is very old and has never been dated. It is a male tree, still hollow, and it stands inside a low wall south-south-east of the church.

faq.q: Where is the yew at Compton Dundon?
faq.a: Inside a low wall south-south-east of St Andrew's church, in the open churchyard.

faq.q: Can I get there by bus?
faq.a: Buses between Street and Somerton run through Compton Dundon; check the current timetable. There is no railway.

trees.story:
Edmund Rack measured this yew in the 1780s, and in the 230 years since, on paper, it has barely changed. Rack, who surveyed the churchyard before his death in 1787, called it a very old yew with a fine top, and noted that the body was hollow and 23 feet round. Tim Hills found 24 feet 9 at ground level in 2000. Peter Norton measured 23 feet 9 in 2014. Different heights, different tapes, and still the same tree within a foot or two.

That stillness is why nobody can tell you its age from its waist. The Ancient Yew Group's figure is 742 centimetres at 30 centimetres off the ground, and yews of this size fall in its class of probably over 800 years, an estimate from girth and not a dating. Locally it was credited with about 1,000 years, the rector Rev. R. Kelland recorded in 1954. Wikipedia goes further, over 1,700, with nothing behind the number. We give you all three and the honest answer, which is that it is very old and undated.

It is a male tree, still hollow, standing inside a low wall to the south-south-east of St Andrew's. Rack would recognise it.

Kelland recorded in 1954 that locally it was credited with about 1,000 years. Wikipedia assesses it over 1700 years (unsourced popular figure). Male tree. Alive: remeasured 2014.
